full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. Both these Civil Appeals, by leave, have been directed against the judgment and order dated 15.06.2014 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.651 of 2012, disposing of the Rule upon declaring the promotions made on 27.12.2011 to the post of Assistant manager from junior Assistant Manager-1 at Dhaka Electric Supply Company Ltd (DESCO) through viva examinations dated 26.12.2011 and 27.12.2011 as being malafide, unlawful and, as such, without any legal effect with direction upon the DESCO to take necessary legal steps for giving promotions afresh in the said posts from amongst the candidates whose interview letters were issued earlier as per rule 3.7 of the DESCO Rules prevailing before 17.11.2011. 

 3. That the present respondents No. 1 to 73, the Junior Assistant Manager-1 of DESCO, filed the above mentioned writ petition challenging the advertisement published in the Daily "Prothom Alo" on 12.01.2013 vide Memo No. DESCO/ HQ/ ADMIN-A (7)/R-S&/2012 dated 11.01.2012 (Annexure-1 to the writ petition) issued by respondent No. 7, for direct recruitment of some Assistant Managers of DESCO and also seeking direction upon the respondents for promoting the writ-petitioners in the vacant posts of Assistant Manager of DESCO as per Government circular vide SRO No.108-Ain/2011/05. 171.022.01. 00.010.2010 dated 03.05.2011 as well as DESCO Board Resolution Nos. 212 and 213; It is contended inter alia that they are permanent non- cadre employees, working as Junior Assistant Manager-1 in DESCO, a company, owned and con-trolled by the Government of Bangladesh having its own service rules known as the DESCO Service Rules, 2002, framed inconformity with the Government Policy with the approval of its Board of Directors; It is further contended that DESCO being owned and controlled by the Government it is bound to follow the Non-cadre Officers and Employees (Seniority and Promotion) Regulations 2011 framed for the purpose of dealing with seniority and promotion of non-Cadre Officers and employees. Moreover, DESCO being a public body within the meaning of section 2(c) of the Service (Reorganization and Conditions) Act 1975 (1975 Act) it must abide by the provisions of the said Act of 1975. DESCO is also under an obligation to fill up 33% of the available vacant positions of Assistant Managers through promotion from the Junior Assistant Mangers, holding Diploma in Engineering as per circular dated 31.7.1978 issued by the Ministry of Finance. It is also alleged that DESCO did not maintain this ratio earlier in giving promotions from the post of Junior Assistant Manager -1, and as such the writ petitioners filed writ petition No. 7511 of 2009 and obtained a rule nisi. Subsequently, when DESCO verbally assured that it would allow 33% promotion from the post of Junior Assistant Manager-1 to Assistant Manager, the aforesaid rule was allowed to be dis-charged for non-prosecution. But unfortunately such promotions were never given to the writ petitioners. However for the purpose of giving promotion to the employees, DESCO prepared a draft seniority list wherein a total of 199 members, holding the post of Junior Assistant Manager- 1 from technical finance and administrative categories was included. Thereafter pursuant to the consent of the Ministry of Power Energy and Mineral Resources the Board of Directors of DESCO in its 212th board meeting held on 17.11.2011 decided to fill up all the vacant posts of DESCO through 100% departmental promotions just for one time within a period of three months. The Board also resolved to introduce a new marking system for assessing candidates for promotion allocating 75 marks out of 100 marks of average Annual Performance Appraisal Rating (APAR) of 3 immediately preceding years and remaining 25 marks for viva voce exams and /or practical tests. Subsequently, the said marking system was further amended in the 213th board meeting, held on 01.12.2011, resolving 70 in place of 75 marks would be allocated for APAR and the remaining 30 in place of 25 marks be allocated for viva voce examination. The Board in the said meeting further resolved that 33% of the vacant posts would be filled up through departmental promotions and 67% through direct recruitment save and except the posts of Managing Director and Director. It is alleged that this decision was in contravention of the recommendation of the concerned Ministry. However, all on a sudden, by memo dated 22.12.2011, the writ respondents in connivance with some vested quarters having vested interest and ill motive issued 142 interview letters out of 199 Junior Assistant Managers-1 named in the seniority list and asked them to appear in the interview to be held on 26.12.2011 and 27.12.2011. But on 27.12.2001 the writ respondents hastily and most illegally selected 46 out of 142 candidates for pro-motion to the post of Assistant Manager superseding many others. It is also alleged that the scores of 46 so called successful candidates were manipulated and wrongly calculated to inflate their total score which was verbally protested, as well as, the writ petitioners verbally requested the DESCO authority to fully comply with the recommendation of the Ministry and the Regulation, 2011 in filling up the vacant posts by 100% departmental promotion. But the DESCO authority did not listen to such requests and published the impugned advertisement in the daily "Prothom Alo" inviting applications for filling up the remaining 67% vacant posts. Hence the writ petitioners were compelled to file the writ petition and obtained Rule Nisi and stay of the operation of the impugned advertisement. 

 5. However, the writ respondent No. 3 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia that DESCO has been incorporated as a public limited company under the Companies Act, 1994 in November, 1996. It has its own Service Rules named, DESCO Service Rules, approved by the Board of Directors, Organogram, Memorandum & Articles of Association. In respect of appointment and promotion of its employees, the Board is the highest authority of DESCO. It is not a 100% Government owned company and, as such, it is not bound to comply with the rules, orders, decisions and policy of the Government. DESCO prepared a draft seniority list to fill up the vacant posts of Assistant Manager by departmental promotion as per DESCO Rules. Subsequently, it was approved by the Board in the 212th meeting. DESCO has not taken any decision in its 212th Board meeting to fill up the vacant posts by 100% departmental pro-motion for one time within three months. The petitioner earlier filed Writ Petition No. 7511 of 2009 before the High Court Division demanding filling up 33% posts of Assistant Manager from amongst them through promotion, but the petitioners withdrew the aforesaid writ petition. Subsequently, in 206th Board meeting it was resolved that 33% post of Assistant Manager would be filled up by promotion from the post of Junior Assistant Manager-1(JAM-1) having at least five years working experience in the said post and minimum 80% marks on an average in the APAR during the immediate past three consecutive years. The respondents duly issued interview letters to 142 candidates according to the DESCO Rules and eventually, gave promotion to 46 Junior Assistant Manager-1(JAM-1) to the post of Assistant Manager covering the 33% of feeder post, as 137 posts of Assistant Manager were vacant. The petitioners filed Writ Petition No. 651 of 2012 for 100% departmental promotion with malafide intention. It is further stated that the advertisement for the post of Assistant Manager was published for direct recruitment having graduation or equivalent degree in Engineering/MBA/Master Degree in any discipline. The writ petitioners are Diploma Engineers, but they have been trying to grab the posts of B.Sc. Engineers and equivalent degree illegally and as such it is stated that the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order of the High Court Division 41 Assistant Managers of DESCO, whose promotions to the said posts have been declared illegal by the impugned judgment, preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1796 of 2014 and the Managing Director, DESCO preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2117 of 2014 wherein leave was granted giving rise to Civil Appeals No. 134 of 2015 and 135 of 2015. 

 8. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant in Civil Appeal No.134 of 2015 (DESCO) submits that the High Court Division erred in law in travelling beyond the scope of Rule Nisi issuing order and thereby declaring the promotions of Junior Assistant Manager-1 to the post of Assistant Managers unlawful and illegal, and thereby holding that the entire promotion process was malafide and tainted with fraud and as such unlawful. He submits that the High Court Division did not take into consideration that the writ-petitioners would also be considered for promotions to the higher posts of Assistant Managers in accordance with DESCO's Service Rules when new vacancy would be created. Mr. Alam further submits that the High Court Division was totally wrong in finding malafide or biasness in the process of promotion to the post of Assistant Manager as there was no such material on record. Mr. Alam also submits that some Junior Assistant Managers-1(JAM-1) were promoted to the posts of Assistant Managers following the relevant Rules long before and as such the High Court Division committed illegality in cancelling the said promotion orders long after TA years of the said promotion orders. The High Court Division has failed to take into consideration the fact that the promotion was not given entirely on the viva-voce marks, rather both the viva-voce marks and the APAR were considered for the said purpose. There may be some errors in summing up the marks, due to inadvertence, but such error does not reflect any significant change nor would make the writ petitioners qualified for promotion. Even if it is admitted, that there are errors in summing up or calculation that is not sufficient to render all the promotions ineffective. Such allegation of error in marking, if any, is a disputed question of fact which cannot be resolved in writ jurisdiction. Hence the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. 

 10. Mr. Ajmalul Hossain, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the present respondents in both the appeals submits that the High Court Division did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned judgment and order because the entire process of interview and promotion was manipulated only to give promotion in the post of Assistant Manager to the people of the appellants authority's choice by victimizing and depriving the writ petitioner-respondents. He further submits that the entire process of promotion was tainted with fraud inasmuch as to promote the appellants of CA No. 135 of 2015 the DESCO Board introduced a new marking system in violation of the provision of Rule 3.7 of the DESCO Service Rules defying the earlier resolution of the Board and thereby to promote them. Accordingly time and again the viva voce marking system was changed and as such when all these serious irregularities and fraudulent activities were detected by the High Court Division it had no other option but to declare the entire promotion process illegal as fraud vitiates everything. In respect of the allegation of the appellants in CA No.135 of 2015 that the High Court Division going beyond the terms of the Rule issuing order declared the promotion of the appellants to be illegal, Mr. Hossain submits that under judicial review the High Court Division can pass any order for ends of justice even by moulding prayer. Thus when such serious irregularities and practicing fraud came to the notice of the High Court Division, it lawfully declared the entire process of promotion of the said appellants as illegal and malafide and as such the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is in accordance with law and as such is liable to be affirmed. 

 11. On consideration of the submissions of the learned Counsel of all the parties and on perusal of the materials on record it appears that admittedly respondents No. 1 to 73 herein, are Junior Assistant Manager-1 (JAM-I) of DESCO. They challenged advertisement dated 12.01.2013 published vide Memo No. DESCO/ HQ/ ADMIN-A (7)/R-S &/2012 dated 11.01.2012 (Annexure-1 to the writ petition) issued by respondent No. 7, for direct recruitment to the post of Assistant Managers of DESCO and also sought direction upon the respondents for their promotion in those vacant posts of Assistant Manager as per Government circular vide SRO No.108-Ain/2011/05 dated 03.05.2011 and DESCO Board Resolution Nos. 212 and 213. It appears that the High Court Division disposed of the Rule by the impugned judgment declaring the promotion dated 27.12.2011 of some Junior Assistant Manager-1(JAM-1) to the post of Assistant Managers, unlawful and illegal, holding that the entire promotion process was malafide and tainted with fraud. Accordingly, DESCO was directed to take necessary steps afresh for promotion to the said posts in accordance with law from amongst the candidates whose interview letters were issued earlier following rule 3.7 of the DESCO Rules as prevalent before 17.11.2011 on the basis of merit-cum-seniority, without any favouritism, nepotism or dictation by any quarter, with-in three months from the date of receipt of the copy of the judgment. 

 11. In the said judgment though the High Court Division, did not declare the impugned memo dated 11.1.2012 and the advertisement published on 12.1.2012 for recruitment to the posts of Assistant Manager of DESCO(Annexure-A) illegal but made the following observations: 

 .............admittedly, DESCO filled up 2/3rd i.e. 67% of the posts of Assistant Manager by direct recruitment leaving 33% post for promotion to the said post." 

 "from paragraph 12 of the supplementary affidavit dated 30.07.2013, it is evident that the petitioners' claim was for filling up 33% posts of Assistant Manager by promotion from amongst JAM-1. Admittedly, 33% posts were not filled up by direct recruitment. Therefore, it cannot be said that direct recruitment of graduate Engineers/MBA, etc. leaving 33% posts for departmental promotion is unlawful." 

 ".... it is evident that the entire promotion process was made in a hurried manner absolutely to favour some persons of the choice of DESCO to give promotion to the posts of Assistant Manager by giving higher marks in viva and thereby, unfairly excluding some of the candidates having seniority as well as higher APAR with malafide intention and ulterior motive. The above facts clearly indicate that the committee was formed solely with the purpose and goal to give promotion on the basis of impropriety, unfairness and malafide. DESCO in order to give white wash to the promotion process called for interview of 142 candidates with new marking system only with a view to promote the persons of DESCO's choice. Therefore, taking interview of the petitioners without any genuine intention to promote them but to pro-mote the candidates of DESCO's choice is not only malafide, but also tainted with fraud upon the petitioners. Thus, from the facts and circumstances, it is evident that the earlier promotion process was malafide tainted with fraud as well as unlawful. In case of promotion of JAM-1 candidates to the post of Assistant Manager, the previous rule 3.7 of the DESCO Rules i.e. merit cum seniority had to be followed." 

 "I. For that the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and order declaring the promotion of the petitioners to the post of Assistant Managers to be unlawful and without jurisdiction should be set aside inasmuch that the terms of the rule nisi issued in Writ Petition No. 651 of 2012 did not entail/cover the lawfulness of the petitioner's promotions. 

 "Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned advertisement bearing Memo No. DESCO/ HQ/Admin-A(7)/R-7/2012 dated 11.01.2012 published in the daily "prothom Alo" dated 12.01.2012 by respondent No.7(Annexure-A), so far as it relates to serial No.1 thereof, for recruitment in the vacant post of Assistant Manager in the Dhaka Electric Supply Company Limited (DESCO), should not be declared to have been issued and published without lawful authority and of no legal effect, and further to show cause as to why direction should not be given upon the respondents to take necessary steps for promoting the petitioners in the vacant post of Assistant Manager of Dhaka Electric Supply Company Limited(DESCO) pursuant to Government Circular being SRO No. 108-Ain/2011/05. 171.022.01.00. 010.2010 dated 03.05.2010 dated 03.05.2011 and DESCO Board Resolution No. 212 dated 17.11.2011 and Resolution No. 213 dated 12.5 .2011(Annexure-C, E and F respectively) and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper". 

 15. From the above it is clear that the Rule was issued to determine firstly, why the impugned advertisement pursuant to memo dated 11.1.2012 for direct appointment to the post of Assistant Manager should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect and secondly, why direction should not be given to take necessary steps for promoting the writ petitioners in the vacant posts of Assistant Managers. 

 16. On perusal of the materials on record it appears that the High Court Division, while passing the impugned judgment, found the first part of the Rule, relating to "publishing the advertisement" has become infractuous due to completion of appointment by direct recruitment in 67% of the vacant posts and as such in the name of consequential relief it declared the entire process of promotion to the post of Assistant Manager, illegal and without lawful authority, although Rule was not issued on the entire promotion process concerning promotion, dated 27.12.2011, of the appellants of CA No. 135 of 2015, or any such prayer being specifically made in the writ petition. 

 "since no vires of law was challenged in this case before the High Court Division and no Rule was issued to that effect the framing of issue No. (II) and conclusion arrived at in (d) and (e) of the judgment are uncalled for being beyond the prayers in the petition and terms of the Rule and these questions were not necessary for disposal of the question whether or not sanction or approval given by the appellants in Annexure-C to the writ petition." 

 20. Of course it is not denied that the High Court Division has discretionary power to grant consequential relief. But the same is to be granted on the basis of the main prayer and according to the terms of the Rule. But in the present case the promotion, dated 27.12.2011 of the present appellants to the post of Assistant Manager from the post of Junior Assistant Manager-1, has not been challenged and no such prayer to that effect has been made in the writ petition nor Rule has been issued to that effect. Had there been such prayer and Rule being issued accordingly, then the High Court Division, after declaring the promotion of 41 appellants illegal, could pass direction upon the authority, in the name of consequential relief, to give promotion to the writ petitioners even if the writ petitioners failed to make such prayer for promoting them in their vacant posts. But in the present case the scenario is quite different. The direction given by the High Court Division, in the name of consequential relief, is not at all acceptable. If that be allowed then flood gates would be open causing anarchy in the administration of justice encouraging many others to get relief, without making any specific prayer before the Court. 

 22. In the instant case, the first part of the Rule is regarding memo dated 11.1.2012 and the advertisement for direct recruitment dated 12.1.2012 and the 2nd part of the Rule is regarding direction to give promotion to the writ petitioners to tile post of Assistant Manager. If, along with the existing first part of the Rule there would have been a prayer against the promotion of the present appellants and if such promotion would have been declared illegal then as consequential relief or ancillary relief direction could have been given to the writ respondents to promote the writ petitioners to the said posts of Assistant Managers. As such the impugned judgment and order is not tenable in the eye of law. 

 23. Now comes the 2nd question as to whether the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and order in violation of the principles of natural justice. In this respect having gone through the writ petition it appears that the appellants alleged that they were not made parties in the writ petition, nor any rule nisi was issued upon them asking or giving them an opportunity of being heard or to present their cases which appears to be correct. As such by making such declaration in the name of consequential relief, the promotion of the present appellants have been cancelled without making them parties and in absence of any such prayer against them or issuing /serving any Rule upon them asking them or giving them opportunity to defend themselves. Under the circumstances as stated above, since the entire promotion process has been found and declared to be malafide and thereby the promotion dated 27.12.2011 of the present appellants of Civil Appeal No. 135 of 2015, have been declared unlawful, and illegal it is clear that the principle of natural justice has been violated. "Natural justice is pervasive facet of secular law where spiritual touch enlivens legislation, administration and adjudication to make fairness a creed of life. It has many colours and shades, many forms and shapes and save where valid law excludes, it applies when people are affected by acts of authority. It is the bone of healthy government recognized from the earliest times and not mystic tantamount of Judge made law." Krishna Iyar J. observed in the case of Mohinder Sing Vs. Chief Election Commissioner (AIR 1978 SC 851). 

 26. Be that as it may, considering the submission made by Mr. Alam that the High Court Division did not take into consideration that 'the writ-petitioners would also be considered for promotion to the higher posts of Assistant Managers in accordance with DESCO's Service Rules when new vacancy would be created' and considering the fact that 67% of the vacant posts have already been filled up by way of direct recruitment on 27.12.2011, we are of the view that the remaining 33% posts of Assistant Managers should be kept reserved to be filled up by promotions from the writ petitioners in accordance with law as well as pursuant to Board's decision dated 1.12.2001.
